title: Automated Motion Tracking and Data Extraction for Red Blood Cell Biomechanics
protocol: Remove static objects from the video.
Apply a filter to the video for noise reduction.
Adjust contrast to accurately analyze cell shapes.
Extract data using the Motion Tracking feature in Basic Protocol 2.
Visualize microfluidic flow at 40× using a Leica DMi8 Inverted Microscope.
Capture videos as .cine files using a Phantom 410-L camera.
Convert captured .cine files to high-quality .avi files for compatibility with Image-Pro 10.
Import .avi video files into Image-Pro 10.
Double-click the red “Uncalibrated” text in the lower right corner of Image-Pro 10.
Set spatial calibration to 1.9001 pixels per unit (micrometer).
Calculate spatial calibration based on magnification and resolution of images.
Set units to microns under the Process tab's Spatial Calibration options.
Calculate the number of pixels/unit based on image resolution and microscope magnification.
Select Average Global for Method and 15 for Size in the Subsample drop-down menu.
Click on the Motion Detect button to generate subsampled images displaying only moving cells.
Under the Process tab, click on 2D Filters.
Open Enhancements menu.
Select Low-Pass filter with Kernel size 5 × 5, Strength 100, and 1 Pass.
Click Apply.
Mix homogenous regions of similar pixel intensity to emphasize biological cells.
Smooth the edges of the cells using a low pass filter to enhance their shapes for segmentation.
Set Black Level (BL) to 109 in the Display section under the Adjust tab.
Set White Level (WL) to 132 in the Display section under the Adjust tab.
Click Apply after setting the Black and White Levels.
Select a Region of Interest (ROI) on enhanced images within Image-Pro software.
Choose tracking options for motion tracking the cells and extracting data.
Navigate to Select tab.
Select Rectangle Tool in the Regions of Interest section.
Draw a rectangular Region of Interest around the microfluidic channels.
Click on the Features Manager button to save an ROI.
Under the Measure tab, click on Objects.
The Motion Tracking tab will appear.
In Segmentation Tracks section, click on Manual button.
Set End value to 123 in the Threshold Tool.
Segment the cells by setting threshold from 0-123.
Under the Motion Tracking tab, click on Types.
Add Regions: Axis, Major, Tracking: Velocity, and Tracking: X Coord.
Click on Edit Range.
Set Minimum and Maximum for Regions: Axis, Major to 7 and 15, respectively.
Select measurement types including velocity, x-coordinates, circularity, area, and major axis length.
Set Minimum and Maximum length to 7 and 15 μm under the Auto Tracking section.
Set Minimum total track length to 600.
Begin auto tracking.
Find Segmentation Tracks section under the Motion Tracking tab.
Click Auto All.
Click Yes on the dialog box that appears, ensuring cells are outlined in red.
Wait for the process completion and note the number of tracked objects displayed in the final dialog box.
Under Data Views, click Data Table button.
Export data by clicking on the arrow near the Excel icon and selecting a file format from the drop-down menu.
